# Add a Global Mute to Weakaura / Weakaura Groups

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/issues/5040
- State: closed (completed)
- Author: intentionaltypos
- Created: 2024-05-01T15:59:30Z
- Updated: 2024-10-31T18:12:21Z
- Repository: WeakAuras/WeakAuras2
- Number: #5040
- Comments: 5
- Closed by: https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/commit/22013e05c88e308bdd1751598f8b0e74ce23be1b

## Labels

- 🎨 Feature Request

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I find it incredibly distracting and frustrating whenever a weakaura makes a sound, which seems to have become the default with the rise of custom sounds / text to speech as an option.  

I've tried to manually delete sounds whenever a pack adds them, but with the options spread across actions, conditions, and various custom options it has become increasingly difficult manually silencing each weak aura.
This becomes even trickier as each time you upgrade a weakaura, many of these deleted are recreated and it becomes a chore to silence pack every time you upgrade. 

I'd love if it there was a way to globally mute weakauras, whether that is across the addon or for specific weakauras.  

I find it particularly strange that weakauras (the addon) can tell me that a particular aura makes sound, but doesn't let me easily silence it. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'm really open to any solution here, such as a global `/wa mute` option, the ability to just click on the sound / TTS icon under a weak aura to mute it, or a right click option a weakaura to mute it.  

Bonus points if this persists through weakaura updates, but if it becomes a simple right click / click, that's still way better than going through hundreds of weakauras disabling actions and conditions.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

...

> So I didn't add a "mute" button after all. The complexity of having another layer to the sound settings didn't seem warranted to me.
> 
> Instead there's now a menu on clicking on the sound icon, which allows for removing all sounds from a group (and its children).
> Obviously those come back when updating, but a) removing them again is pretty quick and b) update should ideally take into account that all sounds were removal locally and not readd them.

**intentionaltypos** commented on 2024-10-31T18:12:20Z:

> I actually saw that in the recent patch notes.  Seems like a great solution.  Thanks for the feature!

# Mute Annoying WoW Sounds Popular! (More than 5000 hits)

Version: BFAv8.3.1

by: [**kiingz**](https://www.wowinterface.com/forums/member.php?s=b77700e8575f98164bca5ae53f509a77&action=getinfo&userid=246208) [ [More](https://www.wowinterface.com/downloads/author-246208.html) ]

This addon will mute some of the annoying sounds of WoW. If you are updating from version 8.1 or lower please read the 8.2 section as the installation instructions have changed.  
  
**Changes in patch 8.2**  
Patch 8.2 broke the way this addon originally worked and so has had to be reworked.  
This addon is now installed into the Interface > Addons directory just like any other addon.  
  
Since this change required a complete rework of the addon there are around ~2500 sounds missing from this version that the previous version muted.  
  
You can safely delete the old versions installation folder "Sound" in your World of Warcraft directory.  
  
This version only works on Retail.
**Custom Sound Mutes:**  
If you want to mute sounds that aren't already included in the addon I've created a small tool to help you do so using sound ids found on wowhead.  
  
To clarify, **this is NOT needed to make this addon work** , this is something extra and entirely optional for those who'd like to mute sounds not already included.  
  
The download and instructions for using it can be found here:  
<https://github.com/Kiingy/MuteWoWSounds>  
  
The above link also contains the complete source code for anyone interested.

\- Classes: Select sounds like Path of Frost, Fan of Kives, mage armors & portals, hunter pet calls, shaman shields and spell cast fizzles.  
\- Mechanical Mounts: Choppers, Flying Machines, Goblin Trikes, Mechastriders and Rockets.

no one reads the release notes :(  
  
I changed DBM to use Master channel as most addon authors did. But i actually added an option in the addon to disable master channel usage and still go through SFX channel. But keep in mind DBM always used master volume until blizzard broke it in 4.0.1.
This is not something we just mindlessly threw in there. There were iiterally hundreds of complaints that 4.0.1 made dbm sounds hard to hear over noisey sound effects, or unable to have dbm sounds when game sounds were off. Using the master channel firstly enables you to have addon sounds even if you turn regular sound effects off, and secondly, makes sure you can hear an addon alert sound over your reduced SFX volume, so a priests portal sound for example cover up an important sound event.  
  
The fact that it's TOO loud has nothing to do with dbm and everything to do with you blasting your computer speakers cause your game isn't configured properly. It just means you have your game sounds turned so low that you over crank your speakers. What you need to do is turn those speakers down, and turn SFX up. or if you don't like dbm using master channel, just click the checkbox in options, it's that simple.
here is a quote from DBM notes which were right on curse download page and homepage main page right on top.  
  
"Now supports playing sound files through "Master" sound channel (making dbm basically function as it did in 3.3.5 with sounds.)  
Added option to disable "Master" channel usage though in case some have gotten used to sounds going through SFX channel since 4.0.1"

excerpts:
* \*\*Immersion & Exploration Addons\*\* — For when you want to enjoy the world
* \*\*Bag & Inventory Management\*\* — Because your bags are probably a disaster
* \*\*Hidden Gems\*\* — Lesser-known addons the community swears by
* \*\*The Future of Addons\*\* — What the Midnight restrictions mean for you

Let’s dive in.

— -

## Part 1: Essential Combat Addons (The Non-Negotiables)

These are the addons I literally cannot imagine playing without. If you’re doing any group content — dungeons, raids, PvP — these should be your first downloads.

## 1\. WeakAuras

What it does: WeakAuras is essentially a blank canvas that lets you create (or import) custom visual and audio alerts for literally anything in the game.

Why it’s essential: Here’s the thing — WeakAuras is simultaneously the most powerful and most intimidating addon in WoW. I remember staring at the configuration screen for the first time and feeling like I needed a computer science degree just to make my cooldowns glow.

...

My Experience: I was convinced I was playing my rotation correctly for months. Then I actually looked at my Details! breakdown and realized I was letting one of my DoTs fall off constantly. Fixed that, saw a 12% DPS increase. The numbers don’t lie.

Important Note: Blizzard is developing their own damage meter for the base UI, but as of the current alpha, it’s not finished. Details! remains the gold standard, and the developer community expects it to continue functioning, though potentially with some limitations on what data it can access.

— -

## 3\. BigWigs/LittleWigs (or Deadly Boss Mods)

What it does: Provides timers, alerts, and warnings for boss abilities in raids and dungeons.

Why it’s essential: Here’s a controversial take: Blizzard designs encounters \*expecting\* you to have a boss mod installed. The visual and audio cues in the base game are often insufficient for the speed at which mechanics happen, especially in Mythic content.
BigWigs (for raids) and LittleWigs (for dungeons) give you:

* Countdown timers for major abilities
* Proximity warnings
* Audio alerts for mechanics targeting you
* Pull timers for coordinating with your group

BigWigs vs. DBM: I’ve used both extensively. BigWigs tends to be lighter weight and more customizable, while DBM is more “plug and play” with louder, more obvious warnings. Neither is objectively better — it’s personal preference. I switched to BigWigs after DBM’s voice alerts started giving me anxiety dreams.

— -

## 4\. Plater Nameplates

What it does: Completely overhauls enemy nameplates with customizable colors, cast bars, and threat indicators.

Why it’s essential: The default Blizzard nameplates are… fine. They work. But Plater transforms them into an actual information system.

With Plater, you can:

* Color-code enemies based on threat status
* Highlight important casts you need to interrupt
* Show debuffs and DoTs on nameplates

...

Why it’s essential: Plumber started as an addon to help with the Emerald Dream seeds in Dragonflight, but it’s evolved into a Swiss Army knife of quality-of-life improvements.

It fixes:

* Auto-loot delays
* Talking head annoyances
* Various UI bugs Blizzard hasn’t addressed

As one Reddit user put it: “I think the dev of Plumber deserves a Nobel Peace Prize.” I’m not sure I’d go that far, but I also haven’t disabled it since I installed it.

Pro Tip: Check the addon options (Options → Addons → Plumber) to customize which features you want enabled. Some overlap with other addons, so you might want to disable certain modules.

— -

## 7\. TomTom

What it does: Creates custom waypoints and an arrow pointing you toward your destination.

Why it’s essential: Every single coordinate on Wowhead has a “TomTom command” option. Click it, paste in chat, press enter, and suddenly you have an arrow pointing exactly where you need to go.

This is especially valuable for:
* Finding rare spawns
* Locating treasures
* Navigating to specific quest objectives
* Finding that one NPC in a city you’ve never been to

My Experience: I spent 20 minutes running around Valdrakken looking for a vendor before I realized I could just TomTom the coordinates. Never again.

— -

## 8\. Leatrix Plus

What it does: A comprehensive quality-of-life addon that consolidates dozens of small improvements.

Why it’s essential: Instead of installing 15 different micro-addons, Leatrix Plus handles:

* Faster auto-loot
* Auto-repair at vendors
* Auto-sell junk items
* Muting annoying sounds (goodbye, “CITIZENS OF DALARAN”)
* Square minimap option
* Maximum camera distance
* Hiding talking heads
* Auto-accepting invites from friends/guild

The Key Feature: That sound muting option alone is worth the download. If you’ve ever wanted to mute the train sound from the toy or the constant voice lines from certain NPCs, Leatrix Plus is your salvation.

— -

## 9\. Easy Delete Confirm

...

* Profession leveling paths

My Experience: When I came back for The War Within after a break, I had no idea what was going on with the story or where to start. Zygor’s guide walked me through everything without me having to watch 45 minutes of “catch-up” YouTube videos. It’s particularly valuable for alts — I’ve leveled 8 characters to max, and the time savings add up significantly.

Who it’s for: New players, returning players, altoholics, achievement hunters, and anyone who values their time. If you’ve ever spent 20 minutes trying to figure out where a quest objective is, this addon pays for itself immediately.

— -

## 11\. Achievements Back Button

What it does: Adds a “back” button to the achievement window.

Why it’s essential: This is one of those “why isn’t this in the base game?” addons.

...

DialogueUI is the more recent option with a cleaner look, while Immersion has been around longer and has more customization options.

— -

## 15\. HandyNotes

What it does: Adds markers to your map showing the locations of treasures, rares, secrets, and collectibles.

Why it’s essential: HandyNotes is actually a framework — you install the base addon and then add expansion-specific plugins (HandyNotes: Dragonflight, HandyNotes: The War Within, etc.).

Once installed, your map lights up with:

* Treasure chest locations
* Rare spawn points
* Secret finding guides
* Achievement-related locations
* Battle pet locations

Important: You need both the base HandyNotes addon AND the specific expansion plugins. This trips up a lot of people.

— -

## 16\. Lorekeeper

What it does: Saves in-game book text so you can read it later without keeping the item.

Why it’s essential: WoW has an incredible amount of lore hidden in books scattered throughout the world. The problem?

...

## 18\. Opie

What it does: Creates radial menus (ring keybindings) for abilities, items, mounts, and toys.

Why it’s essential: Opie is one of those addons that sounds unnecessary until you use it. Instead of dedicating keybinds to situational abilities, you create rings that pop up on a single keybind.

Example setup:

* One key for a ring containing all your mounts
* One key for a ring with all your professions
* One key for utility abilities you don’t use in combat

My Experience: I freed up about 8 keybinds by moving rarely-used abilities to Opie rings. My action bars are cleaner, and I still have quick access to everything.

— -

## 19\. FarmHud

What it does: Turns your minimap into a transparent radar overlay around your character.

Why it’s essential: If you do any gathering (mining, herbalism, skinning), FarmHud is incredible. Instead of constantly looking at the corner of your screen, the minimap becomes a transparent overlay centered on your character.

...

Based on conversations with addon developers (including members of the WeakAuras core team), here’s the situation:

What Blizzard Says They Want:

* Eliminate addons that “solve” boss mechanics automatically
* Remove “cybernetic enhancements” that tell you exactly what button to press
* Create a more level playing field between addon users and non-users
* Improve the new player experience by reducing addon dependency

What’s Actually Being Restricted:

* Access to certain spell and cooldown information
* The ability for addons to “see” certain game states
* Computational logic that can make decisions for players

The Developer Perspective:

As one WeakAuras developer told me: “It’s 100% different from what they said they were going to do and what we expected them to do. They said in interviews this would be a slow process, but they just got into the bulldozer and drove over the whole thing.”
